title: Hangs and hitches (UI responsiveness)
summary: A hang is when the app does not respond to touches for 250 ms or more. A hitch is a frame shown late, which looks like stutter. Both come from too much work on the main thread.
body: **In simple words:** Hang = "I tapped and nothing happened". Hitch = "scrolling is jerky". Same root cause: the main thread is busy.

**Usual causes:** synchronous file, database or Keychain access on main; big JSON decoding on main; Core Data fetches on the main context; image decoding; heavy layout; main thread waiting on a lock held by a background thread; `DispatchQueue.main.sync` from background.
**Find in development:** Thread Performance Checker (Xcode warnings), Instruments (Hangs, Time Profiler, Animation Hitches).
**Find in production:** Xcode Organizer hang reports with stack traces, MetricKit `MXHangDiagnostic`, and hitch-rate metrics (ms of hitch per second of scrolling).
**Fix:** move work off main (async functions marked `@concurrent`, background contexts), precompute and cache formatted values, load data incrementally, avoid main waiting for low-priority work.
**Staff angle:** dashboards for hang rate and hitch rate per screen and release, owners per screen, alerts on regressions during phased rollout.
keyPoints: Hang ≥ 250 ms unresponsive; hitch = late frame.
Root cause is main-thread work: I/O, decoding, heavy layout, lock contention.
Dev tools: Thread Performance Checker, Instruments. Field: Organizer, MetricKit.
Hitch rate = hitch time / scroll time; track per screen.
Fix by moving work off main and doing less per frame.

followups: **User says "the app freezes on the home screen sometimes". How do you investigate?** Check Organizer hang reports for that screen, reproduce with Time Profiler, look for sync I/O or locks on main, fix, verify hang rate drops in the next release.
